title: Closure Captures Binding: Scope Ends, Lifetime Continues
description: make_adder returns adder closure that captures n. Scope of n is make_adder's body only, but lifetime extends as long as closure exists. Two closures add5 and add10 each capture their own n (5 and 10). __closure__ inspection shows cell_contents 5 and 10.
source: draft: omp free model + edit: codex

steps.description: make_adder(n) defines inner adder(x) returning x + n. n is local to make_adder (scope), but adder captures it. Return adder function.
Comment: n's scope is make_adder body; n's lifetime is as long as returned closure exists. Closure keeps binding alive after scope ends.
add5 = make_adder(5), add10 = make_adder(10). Two separate closures, each with its own captured n.
make_adder has returned, its scope gone. But add5(3) = 8 (5+3), add10(3) = 13 (10+3). n values still alive.

steps.question: Why does add5(3) return 8 even though make_adder finished executing?
steps.answer: The closure captures the binding of n, keeping it alive. The cell containing 5 persists as long as add5 exists.

steps.description: Inspect closure cells: add5.__closure__[0].cell_contents = 5, add10.__closure__[0].cell_contents = 10. Direct proof of captured values.
Output: 8 and 13  -  closures use their captured n values.
Output: 5 and 10  -  cell contents show each closure captured its own n.
